date_note: Date is the intrusion as reported by Dailysecu and ZDNet Korea (around 23:42 KST on 16 November); the university confirmed it on 17 November.
title: Jeonju University says hack of its AHA education service leaked student and staff records
summary: Dailysecu and ZDNet Korea report that Jeonju University's online liberal-arts service "AHA" was hacked around 23:42 KST on 16 November and the university confirmed it on 17 November. About 180,000 records of students, graduates and staff leaked, about 25,000 with resident registration numbers; Dailysecu notes records are not people. The university halted the service and reported to the PIPC, KISA and the Ministry of Education; the cause is under investigation.

evidence.quote: 전주대 온라인 교양 교육과정 서비스 시스템이 해킹돼 학생과 교직원 등의 개인정보 18만여 건이 유출됐다.
이 가운데 2만5000여 건에는 주민등록번호가 포함된 것으로 확인됐다.

plain: Jeonju University in South Korea says a hack of its online AHA education service leaked about 180,000 records, about 25,000 including resident registration numbers. It has told those affected.
exec: A university web service holding student, graduate and staff data was breached; check which small online services hold national ID numbers.
action: Jeonju University urges people to change any password reused from its old website, check the 'personal information leak lookup' on its site, and, if their resident registration number leaked, watch for identity theft.

sources.name: ZDNet Korea: 전주대, 온라인 교양 시스템 해킹...개인정보 18만건 유출

validation.note: Two independent publishers, ZDNet Korea and Dailysecu, each report the university's statement with the same figures. The university's own notice was not read. Entry route not stated; ZDNet Korea says the cause is under investigation.

review.note: Checked 16/17 Nov dates, about 180,000 records, about 25,000 with RRN, records-not-people caveat, reports to PIPC/KISA/MoE against Dailysecu
